hook: The first jets ever to land on the new carrier John F. Kennedy.
narration: These were the first jets to land on the new carrier John F. Kennedy.
The fighters lined up overhead, waiting for their turn.
Each pilot aims for a short strip of deck that never stops moving.
A hook under the tail grabs a steel cable across the deck and stops the jet in about two seconds.
Then a Super Hornet landed next.
Deck crews in colored jerseys moved in fast to clear the landing area.
outcome: The Kennedy caught its first fixed-wing jets, and the pilots taxied in to a crowd on deck.
title: Carrier Kennedy catches its first jets
question_comment: Would you rather fly the jet or work the deck?

facts.claim: First ever fixed-wing recovery ops, Atlantic, Oct 13 2026
facts.source_quote: Pre-Commissioning Unit John F. Kennedy conducts its first ever flight recovery operations involving fixed-wing aircraft while underway in the Atlantic Ocean, Oct. 13, 2026.

facts.claim: Ship was testing its launch and recovery equipment
facts.source_quote: John F. Kennedy is underway conducting Aircraft Compatibility Testing, which assess the operational capabilities of the ship's aircraft launch and recovery equipment with U.S. Navy aircraft.
